entities.name: War of the League of Cambrai
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The War of the League of Cambrai was a pivotal conflict in the Italian Wars of 1494-1559, distinguishing itself as the first time a coalition of states formed against the Venetian Republic. 

This complex and multifaceted event took place in the Iberian Peninsula, specifically in present-day Spain and Portugal, from 1508-02-01 to 1516-12-01. 

At its core, the War of the League of Cambrai was a clash of interests between the Holy Roman Empire, the Papal States, and the Kingdom of France, pitted against the Venetian Republic and its allies. 

The conflict had far-reaching consequences, including the shifting of the balance of power in Europe and the eventual decline of the Venetian Republic as a major world power. 

As the great historian and diplomat Niccolò Machiavelli observed, 'The war was a great test of the strength and courage of the Italian states, and it showed that they were not yet capable of defending themselves against the might of the great powers of Europe.'
